# Incident Report: 2022-01-07 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim host
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | 192.168.1.216 |
| MAC | 9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9 |
| Hostname | DESKTOP-GXMYNO2 (domain SPOONWATCH.NET, workgroup name SPOONWATCH) |
| Logged-in user | steve.smith |

Confirmed by: ARP/Ethernet binding IP↔MAC, DHCP request (option 12/61 `DESKTOP-GXMYNO2`), and Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString `steve.smith` / `DESKTOP-GXMYNO2$` against realm SPOONWATCH.NET.

## Malware family
**Information stealer, behaviorally consistent with Vidar/Arkei-family stealer** (Redline/Vidar-class credential and browser-data stealer). **Attribution: behavioral**, not signature-confirmed — no IDS/Suricata alert export was included in the evidence directory, only the pcap and pre-exported HTTP objects. The finding rests on traffic behavior, not a named detection signature.

Behavioral basis:
- At t=203s the host makes 7 back-to-back HTTP POSTs to a bare IP (`2.56.57.108`, no DNS lookup precedes it) at `/osk//1.jpg` through `/osk//7.jpg`, each returning a `200 image/jpeg`-labeled response whose body is actually an `MZ` PE32 DLL (confirmed via `file` on the exported objects — mix of GUI/console DLLs).
- This is the classic "fetch helper DLLs disguised as images" stage used by stealers to load the libraries needed to decrypt browser-stored credentials (e.g. SQLite/crypto DLLs for Chrome/Firefox data).
- Immediately after (t=207s), the host POSTs to `/osk/` a 379,629-byte multipart body (`Content-Type: zip`) named `_5861695120.zip`, containing `autofill/Google Chrome_Default.txt`, `screenshot.jpg`, and `system.txt` — textbook stealer exfiltration triad (autofill/credential data, a desktop screenshot, and host/system fingerprint).
- No HTTP User-Agent header is set on any of the malicious requests — consistent with a custom malware HTTP client rather than a browser or legitimate updater.
- Delivery vector is not observable in this capture: the C2 traffic begins ~203 seconds into the capture with no preceding download/dropper traffic, so the initial infection stage (e.g., phishing, cracked-software site) occurred before capture start or off-wire.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint**
- `2.56.57.108:80` — destination of all 9 malicious POSTs (`/osk//1.jpg`–`/osk//7.jpg`, `/osk//main.php`, `/osk/`); no accompanying DNS resolution observed, i.e. hardcoded/bare-IP C2.

**Malicious URLs**
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//1.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//2.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//3.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//4.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//5.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//6.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//7.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//main.php`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk/` (exfiltration endpoint)

**Domains**: none — the C2 was contacted by bare IP with no DNS lookup in the capture.

**Transferred files (malicious payload DLLs downloaded from C2, disguised with .jpg extension) — SHA256**
| Delivered as | SHA256 |
|---|---|
| /osk//1.jpg | a770ecba3b08bbabd0a567fc978e50615f8b346709f8eb3cfacf3faab24090ba |
| /osk//2.jpg | 3fe6b1c54b8cf28f571e0c5d6636b4069a8ab00b4f11dd842cfec00691d0c9cd |
| /osk//3.jpg | 334e69ac9367f708ce601a6f490ff227d6c20636da5222f148b25831d22e13d4 |
| /osk//4.jpg | e2935b5b28550d47dc971f456d6961f20d1633b4892998750140e0eaa9ae9d78 |
| /osk//5.jpg | 43536adef2ddcc811c28d35fa6ce3031029a2424ad393989db36169ff2995083 |
| /osk//6.jpg | c40bb03199a2054dabfc7a8e01d6098e91de7193619effbd0f142a7bf031c14d |
| /osk//7.jpg | 16574f51785b0e2fc29c2c61477eb47bb39f714829999511dc8952b43ab17660 |

Each is a Windows PE32 DLL (GUI or console subtype per `file`), not a real JPEG.

**Exfiltrated data (uploaded from victim to C2)**
- Filename: `_5861695120.zip`, SHA256 `1ecee6ff37e03c1160b8bf66d5ca8dc784e0b35fb9fd105f0964b314d310c07f`
- Contents: `autofill/Google Chrome_Default.txt` (browser autofill data), `screenshot.jpg` (desktop screenshot), `system.txt` (host fingerprint)
- Uploaded via POST to `http://2.56.57.108/osk/` at t=207s, 379,629 bytes.

## Benign context (not indicators)
- `2.56.57.108:80` traffic is the only non-Microsoft, non-AD conversation of note; all other external endpoints (`23.38.189.*`, `52.*`, `20.*`, `204.79.197.*`, `8.253.189.126`, `184.50.62.43`, `40.83.240.146`, `104.212.67.47`) are Windows Update / Delivery Optimization / Microsoft telemetry (`download.windowsupdate.com`, `au.download.windowsupdate.com`, `ctldl.windowsupdate.com`, `settings-win.data.microsoft.com`, `v10/v20.events.data.microsoft.com`, `client.wns.windows.com`), fetching legitimate `.cab`/Defender-update `.exe` files — unrelated background OS noise.
- `192.168.1.2` = internal Active Directory DC (`SPOONWATCH-DC.spoonwatch.net`) — LDAP/Kerberos/SMB/DRSUAPI traffic is normal domain-join/auth chatter.
- mDNS/LLMNR/SSDP/NBNS broadcast traffic is normal LAN discovery noise.

## Incident summary
The Windows workstation DESKTOP-GXMYNO2 (192.168.1.216, MAC 9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9), logged in as domain user steve.smith (SPOONWATCH.NET), was infected with an information-stealer (behaviorally matching the Vidar/Arkei stealer family; attribution is behavioral, not signature-confirmed). Starting ~3.4 minutes into the capture, the malware pulled 7 helper DLLs disguised as `.jpg` files from a hardcoded C2 at 2.56.57.108:80 via the `/osk/` path, then harvested and exfiltrated browser autofill data, a desktop screenshot, and system information as a 379 KB ZIP archive to the same server. No delivery/dropper traffic is present in this capture, so the initial infection vector could not be determined.
